title.narrative: Addressing multifaced humanitarian needs of refugees, IDPs and host communities in Syria and Türkiye

description.narrative: In Syria, the intervention targets mostly Internally Displaces Persons (IDPs) displaced by the earthquake and previously by conflict, those who lost family members, livelihoods or their house during the earthquake, households living under the poverty line, households hosting IDPs, households with children and women at risk, the elderly, and people with disabilities. In Türkiye, specific attention shall be paid to refugee households (both Syrians and other nationalities), mothers and children at risk of malnutrition, displaced people by the earthquake living in formal/informal settings but also those living in the cities and unable to cover their basic needs, including rent , children (especially girls) at risk of violence and school abandonment, people with disabilities. Due to ongoing and escalating social tensions, both displaced and host communities (in a smaller percentage) will be targeted.

Increase access to humanitarian assistance for meeting basic needs through the provision of live-saving support and community based and specialized protection services for at risk and highly vulnerable groups in Syria and Türkiye.

WHH and partners are aiming to provide lifesaving and life sustaining assistance to those vulnerable Households to support them in overcoming both man-made and natural disasters. WHH proposes a three outputs intervention focusing on ensuring access to quality food as well as improving nutritional behaviors, provision of different types of support (shelter rehabilitation and WASH) and community based protection.
